newsitem.title: DUBAI: Moslems begin Ramadan fasting month.
newsitem.headline: Moslems begin Ramadan fasting month.

text.p: Moslems in many countries around the world on Friday observed the start of the fasting month of Ramadan, traditionally a time of abstinence by day and shorter working hours.
During Ramadan the faithful should not eat, drink or smoke in daylight hours. Non-Moslems in Islamic countries are asked to be sensitive by not doing those things in public.
Sensual pleasures such as sex and listening to music are also banned during the day.

In Saudi Arabia, birthplace of Islam in the seventh century and home to its two holiest shrines, the Interior Ministry warned non-Moslems to respect the holy month. It said foreigners eating, drinking or smoking in public during daylight hours would risk deportation and cancellation of their work contracts.
Saudi Arabia has a large expatriate population, many of them labourers from the Indian subcontinent and other Asian states.
The start of the Ramadan usually depends on when the crescent of the new moon is sighted in each country.
Other major Moslem countries where Ramadan started on Friday include Indonesia, Egypt, Syria and Jordan.

In Iran, across the Gulf from Saudi Arabia and the largest country dominated by the minority Shi'ite sect of Islam, Ramadan is set to start on Saturday, provided the new moon is sighted on Friday evening.
The end of Ramadan is marked by the religious feast of Eid al-Fitr which customarily involves the exchange of gifts.
